answer: An agent economy resists sybils by requiring every new identity to lock a kernel stake of 2000 POA that escalates by 1000 for each additional account sharing the same sponsor or key-derivation prefix. Established peers act as a wharf matching half the stake and jointly liable. When a cluster of five or more is detected by graph analysis of entry patterns all linked kernel stakes are made hollow completely and burned so the attacker loses capital proportional to N squared. This makes large farms unprofitable as marginal cost and slash probability rise faster than any parallel reward.
